reviews.review: Only game where I can kill the French big bugs and god at the same time with a giant anime hammer.

Many of these reviews may look like memes, but if you play any EDF game you'll understand why.

This game is the embodiment of Reggie's "If it's not fun, why bother". The game includes over the top weaponry, giant bugs, unrealistic radio chatter, and 4 distinct classes, ensuring that there will be very few dull moments. With all of this in mind, however, I can only recommend the game at full price if you have a minimum of one other friend to play with.  EDF was meant to be played with friends, enabling the usage of various multi seat vehicles and hilarious weaponry and combos that cannot be used solo (look up the Leviathon missile launcher from EDF as an example), while also making sure that your team will always have the tools necessary to deal with the various enemies' strengths and weaknesses. The game can still be a blast if you're playing solo, but I would wait for a sale if you know you'll only play solo. With 4 scaling difficulties and over 100 missions, there is definitely enough content within the game for its hefty price, especially since the crazier weapons may only be unlocked as you spend more time in the game by playing through harder difficulties.

Even EDF has its problems, although they are not enough to outweigh the fun to be had. The Air Raider and Wing Diver classes have rough early games, unlocking pitiful weaponry compared to the other classes. This is mitigated by the unique and powerful equipment they unlock later on, yet these initial unlocks make me recommend new players to play on hard instead of a normal playthrough to accelerate their unlocks and truly feel the EDF experience. Although weapon drops are random to a degree, the problem lies in the random stats that the weapon drops have. This is the only glaring issue this EDF has compared to others, for a more powerful version of a previous weapon can actually be weaker initially due to these random stats. As duplicates are found, these stats upgrade, sort of fixing this problem, but it makes you wonder why it was implemented.

TLDR, If you're looking for an over the top arcade co op shooter that you can play as much as you want alone or (for the best, hilarious experience) with friends, then much fun is to be had with this game. Read the review for the actual negatives, and you'll be prepared to deal with them and enjoy your experience to the maximum when they arise.
